steps.description:
Create a program that performs the following: 1. Ask you to input the number of strings to be entered 2. Ask you to input the strings one by one and append to a list 3. Display the list each time a string is being input.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 3 nothing is impossible

4 dumb is clever too

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input integer: 3 Input string 1: nothing ['nothing'] Input string 2: is ['nothing', 'is'] Input string 3: impossible ['nothing', 'is', 'impossible']

Example 2 Input integer: 4 Input string 1: dumb ['dumb'] Input string 2: is ['dumb', 'is'] Input string 3: clever ['dumb', 'is', 'clever'] Input string 4: too ['dumb', 'is', 'clever', 'too']

Create a program that performs the following: 1. Ask you to input the number of strings to be entered 2. Ask you to input the strings one by one and insert at the front of a list 3. Display the list each time a string is being input.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 3 nothing is impossible

4 dumb is clever too

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input integer: 3 Input string 1: nothing ['nothing'] Input string 2: is ['is', 'nothing'] Input string 3: impossible ['impossible', 'is', 'nothing']

Example 2 Input integer: 4 Input string 1: dumb ['dumb'] Input string 2: is ['is', 'dumb'] Input string 3: clever ['clever', 'is', 'dumb'] Input string 4: too ['too', 'clever', 'is', 'dumb']

The Lab is holding a Coin Shop Bazaar selling extra-ordinary souvenirs. A group of students wanted to visit the bazaar but only those with at least 50 coins can enter. Create a program that performs the following: 1. Enter the number of students in the group. 2. Asks for a name and the number of coins the student has. 3. If the student has at least 50 coins, add the name to a guest list. 4. Repeat step (2) to (3) for the number of students in the group 5. Display the guest list. Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 4 Melvin 33 Joe Chiang 65 Rick Donald 49 Kimberly 50 3 Tommy Gunn 50 Rocky Balboa 51 Martin 50

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Total students: 4 Input name 1: Melvin Input coins: 33 Input name 2: Joe Chiang Input coins: 65 Input name 3: Rick Donald Input coins: 49 Input name 4: Kimberly Input coins: 50 ['Joe Chiang', 'Kimberly']

Example 2 Total students: 3 Input name 1: Tommy Gunn Input coins: 50 Input name 2: Rocky Balboa Input coins: 51 Input name 3: Martin Input coins: 50 ['Tommy Gunn', 'Rocky Balboa', 'Martin']

The Lab is holding a Coin Shop Bazaar selling extraordinary souvenirs. A few groups of students wanted to visit the bazaar but only those with at least 50 coins can enter.

Create a program that performs the following: 1. Enter the number of groups. 2. For each group, perform the following: a. Enter the number of students in the group. b. Asks for a name and the number of coins the student has. c. If the student has at least 50 coins, add the name to a guest list. The same guest list will be used for all groups. d. Repeat steps (b) to (c) for the number of students in the group 5. Display the guest list. Follow the test output display format.
